rubric_title: Customer Support Chatbot with Amazon Bedrock Flows

criteria.section: Build a Bedrock Flow with Classification and Routing
criteria.criterion: Build a Bedrock Flow that classifies customer messages and routes them across distinct paths
learning_objectives: Orchestrate multi-path LLM applications using Bedrock Flows
Design classifier prompts that produce consistent, condition-compatible output
submission_requirements: The flow classifies incoming customer messages into distinct categories
The classifier produces consistent, unambiguous output that can drive routing decisions
Messages are routed to distinct paths based on their category
Distinct paths exist in the flow, each terminating at a separate Output node

pass_if: Messages of different types route to different branches and each path ends at its own Output node
fail_if: The application is implemented as a single path
pass_with_comment_if: Some paths are combined into a single route
praise_if: The flow uses structured output to generate a routing decision

criteria.section: Implement the Bug Report Path Using a Bedrock Agent
criteria.criterion: Implement the bug report path using a Bedrock Agent with a tool to collect information and create tickets
learning_objectives: Configure Bedrock Agents with tools to perform actions on behalf of the user
Collect structured information from users through agent interactions
Implement a feedback loop using a Bedrock agent
submission_requirements: The bug report path includes a Bedrock agent
The agent is configured to invoke the Lambda tool to persist the ticket
The agent collects bug description, steps to reproduce, and environment information from the customer
A record is created in the BugReports DynamoDB table when a bug report message is processed through the flow

pass_if: A bug report message sent through the flow results in a new item in the BugReports DynamoDB table
fail_if: The agent is not connected to the create-bug-report tool
No DynamoDB record is created when a bug report message is sent
pass_with_comment_if: The agent works but does not attempt to collect steps to reproduce or environment — note that these fields improve ticket quality

criteria.section: Implement Platform Question and Other Request Paths
criteria.criterion: Implement paths for platform questions and other customer requests
learning_objectives: Design prompt nodes that answer questions grounded in provided documentation
Handle out-of-scope requests with appropriate redirection
submission_requirements: The application produces a relevant answer when the question is covered by the FAQ
The application directs a user to a support phone number when the question is not covered by the FAQ
A separate path exists for other customer support requests that directs the user to a support phone number

pass_if: A platform question returns an answer drawn from the FAQ content
An off-FAQ question returns a phone number redirect
An other-request message returns a phone number redirect
fail_if: The FAQ path is missing or the FAQ content is not used to answer platform questions
praise_if: The student uses a knowledge base instead of embedding FAQ into a prompt
The application is handling bad requests like a prompt injection attack

criteria.section: Test and Evaluate the Flow Using Automated Tooling and Bedrock Evaluations
criteria.criterion: Test the flow using an automated test suite and evaluate response quality using Bedrock Evaluations with LLM-as-a-judge
learning_objectives: Design test suites that verify routing and response quality
Evaluate LLM application quality using automated evaluation pipelines
submission_requirements: flow-tests.json contains at least one test entry for the bug report path, at least one for the platform question path, and at least one for the other requests path
The generate-eval-dataset.py script is run against the flow and produces a JSONL output file
The JSONL file is uploaded to S3 and a Bedrock Evaluation job is created
The result's correctness score is close to 1

pass_if: The test file covers all three paths, a JSONL file is produced, and an evaluation job exists in the AWS account
fail_if: The test file covers fewer than three paths
The JSONL file is not produced
The result's correctness score is close to 0
pass_with_comment_if: Test scores for some test-cases are low — encourage the student to review reference responses and iterate on prompts
praise_if: The student added edge-case tests such as ambiguous messages or prompt injection attempts

stand_out_suggestions: Add a guardrail to the flow that blocks harmful content and prompt injection attempts before any model processes the message.
Add edge-case test prompts to flow-tests.json: ambiguous messages that could belong to multiple categories, very short messages with minimal context or prompt injection attempts.
Replace the embedded FAQ with a Bedrock Knowledge Base backed by a vector index so the flow can handle a larger document without embedding it in every prompt.
Use structured output to ensure that the classifier node only produces valid values.
